content.text:
I traced the full history of `MinimalImportScanner.java` (the only file whose logic the fix touches) back through its four prior commits.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: ae1aab70789c2cf6874bf5a4a5ec98becc170979

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation.** The fix (9e871e9f) only changes logic in `MinimalImportScanner.shouldTypeBeImported`: it (a) switches `qualifiedNameTokens` from an unordered `HashSet` to an ordered `LinkedList`, (b) checks only the *last* token (`qualifiedNameTokens.getLast()`) against `fieldAndMethodsNames`/`localVariablesOfBlock` instead of iterating over *every* token, and (c) stops the package walk-up at the top-level package. I ran `git log --follow` on the file to get its full history (2709a947 → 37c90f87 → 3eeb6399 → ae1aab70 → 9e871e9f) and then `git blame` on the pre-fix version to attribute each modified line to the commit that last touched it.

**(2) Specific defect.** `git blame` shows the exact line the fix rewrites — `if (fieldAndMethodsNames.contains(token) || localVariablesOfBlock.contains(token))` — was introduced by ae1aab70. Before that commit, the code used a single `namedElements` set that was only populated when the enclosing class matched the scan's `targetType` (a scoping guard). Commit ae1aab70 removed that guard and replaced it with two unconditional, scanner-lifetime-persistent sets: `fieldAndMethodsNames` (populated from *every* `CtField`/`CtMethod` name seen while walking the whole compilation unit) and `localVariablesOfBlock`. Combined with the pre-existing (but now much more dangerous) pattern of testing membership for *every* token of the field's fully-qualified name (including each package segment), this let an unrelated method name elsewhere in the class collide with a package-name segment and produce a false "should import" verdict.

**(3) Evidence.** The regression test added alongside the fix (`DigestUtil`) is a private static field `STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH` used inside `updateDigest()`, in a class that also declares overloaded methods named `digest(...)`. Its package `...testclasses.digest` shares the literal token `"digest"` with those method names. Under the pre-fix code, `fieldAndMethodsNames` (introduced by ae1aab70) picks up `"digest"` while the scanner visits the `digest(...)` methods, and this pollutes the check performed later for the unrelated `STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH` field access, causing Spoon to wrongly emit `import static ...DigestUtil.STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH;` for a field already in scope. This exactly matches the mechanism ae1aab70 introduced (unconditional, cross-cutting `fieldAndMethodsNames`) and that 9e871e9f fixes by restricting the check to the single relevant (last) token.

**Uncertainty:** The surrounding structural weaknesses that the fix also touches — the unordered `Set` for `qualifiedNameTokens` and the "walk up until top package" loop — trace back further, to 2709a947 and 37c90f87 respectively. Those commits built the fragile foundation this bug relies on, but per my analysis they alone (with the `targetType`-scoped guard still in place) would not have produced this specific false positive; ae1aab70's removal of that guard is what most directly enabled it. I was not able to build/run the project to empirically bisect this (restricted to read-only git inspection), so this conclusion is based on static code analysis rather than confirmed execution.
